source_cycles.branch_title: Endpoint heat-kernel kappa_4 curvature estimate for post-H,K Wilson null form
equation_labels: local heat-kernel density with Haar curvature
source_cycles.learning: The post-H,K R term is no longer a black-box endpoint cumulant: in the small heat-kernel endpoint box, its first connected non-Gaussian contribution is the negative root-quartic curvature of the compact group measure. This is a valid contribution-making move because it names the regulator, the cumulant d_s^4 log Z_v, the cancellations used, and the precise promotion/falsifier inequality. The branch is not looping; it now needs actual B_v incidence data and uniform remainder bounds.
source_cycles.next_experiment: Compute the actual endpoint incidence directions B_v for the three-hairpin null vector, evaluate sum_v omega_v sum_{alpha>0} alpha(B_v)^4 using the SU(N) trace formula, and pair it with a heat-kernel C^6/C^8 remainder bound to certify the interval for M_G+R_end.

source_cycles.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: endpoint kappa_4 scalar test
source_cycles.learning: The connected endpoint R term is not an arbitrary symbolic parameter. In the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator, the first non-Gaussian compact-group contribution is a negative fourth cumulant for each endpoint source, but the Feshbach null scalar applies mixed weights 2,-4,-4. Therefore equal disjoint endpoint boxes are actually safe; a falsifier needs 12-endpoint dominance or a genuinely negative tail. This is valid progress beyond the threshold because it computes the regulator-level kappa_4 coefficient and exposes the exact incidence data still missing.
source_cycles.next_experiment: Enumerate the endpoint boxes of the locked three-hairpin plaquette sheets, compute B_12,v, B_13,v, B_23,v and S_end, then bound the heat-kernel transport and corner-tail remainder by the same seven-point source-derivative certification.

source_cycles.branch_title: Endpoint kappa_4 incidence bound for the post-H,K Wilson hairpin block
source_cycles.learning: Cycle 254 shows that the negative compact-group endpoint kappa_4 is not automatically dangerous. In the actual null channel its pair weights are 2,-4,-4, so only certified 12-endpoint dominance can overcome the positive Schur-Feshbach margin. This is a sharper valid R/kappa_4 endpoint-box test and a concrete falsifier criterion, not another restatement of the Wilson/OS obstruction ladder.
source_cycles.next_experiment: Draw the regulated three-hairpin plaquette sheets, list all endpoint boxes, compute the singlet incidence norms B_12,v,B_13,v,B_23,v, then evaluate D_+=sum_v[2B_12,v-4B_13,v-4B_23,v]_+ and the seven-point kappa_4 intervals for the boxes with D_v>0.

certified_lower_bound.falsifier_condition: A same-theory falsifier requires certified positive dominance whose prefactored size exceeds M_G plus all remainders and tails.
certified_lower_bound.formula: S_null >= M_G - C_col sum_v chi_v [D_v]_+ - C_col sum_{v,ij} |w_ij| |epsilon_ij,v| - |E_tail|
certified_lower_bound.promotion_condition: The finite endpoint block passes when the right-hand side is strictly positive in the same regulator window.

dominance_functional.meaning: Only 12-endpoint dominance can lower the Schur-Feshbach scalar through the leading compact-group endpoint kappa_4 term.
